A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RSA2C despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated sections and renumbered results.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original continuous-control and LQR simulations, including returns, computational costs, noise robustness, and attribution analyses.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain these original simulation results, including performance comparisons, robustness evaluations, and LQR convergence curves.

M1.justification: RSA2C retains the same Gaussian RKHS Actor, Value and Advantage Critics, SHAP-weighted kernel, dictionary sparsification, and update procedures. Algorithm 1 and the relocated algorithm derivations describe the same method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Pendulum-v1, BipedalWalker-v3, Ant-v5, and the linearized cart-pole LQR benchmark. Moving the experimental appendix from D to A does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Advanced AC, RKHS-AC, SAC, and PPO, alongside the two RSA2C variants. The LQR comparison retains Advanced-AC; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Environment specifications, hyperparameters in Tables 6–8, five evaluation episodes, return and cost metrics, noise levels, and LQR settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations, state-noise robustness tests, SHAP beeswarm and temporal heatmap analyses, and LQR optimality-gap analysis. These analyses are relocated without new tests.

E5.justification: Both state that curves and tables average over 10 random seeds and retain the same uncertainty bands and mean-plus/minus-standard-deviation reporting. No additional statistical procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The numerical result tables and plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 12 retains zero-noise Ant-v5 returns of 934.15 ± 44.39 for RSA2C-CME and 4477.33 ± 1950.69 for SAC.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 removes v1's allowance that the predictor may merely be approximated in the RKHS, leaving explicit RKHS membership as the stated condition for Equation 2. The convergence bounds and appendix proofs otherwise match after notation changes and relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about attribution-guided kernel Actor-Critic learning, global non-asymptotic convergence under perturbations, efficiency, stability, and interpretability.

C2.justification: v2 strengthens causal interpretations of retained evidence. Appendix A.3 explicitly links SHAP reweighting to resistance to noisy gradients, and A.5.2 primarily attributes improved stability to SHAP. The Ant-v5 representational limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes the reproducibility statement promising an open-source link upon acceptance. Hardware, hyperparameter tables, and algorithm details remain available; this removes future-access information rather than an existing code link.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work themes remain the same. Section 1.2 slightly narrows the explicit research-gap statement by removing sample-complexity bounds from the listed open problems while retaining non-asymptotic convergence guarantees.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: the contents move to the front, experimental Appendix D becomes Appendix A, and the former algorithm appendices are consolidated under Appendix B. It also changes the title, reorganizes proof subsections, and edits prose and disclosures.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography and page geometry throughout, substantially enlarges plots, and redistributes figures and tables across pages. All original displays remain, with some revised captions, including Figures 2 and 3.

improvement.justification: Larger plots, front-positioned contents, and experiments placed before lengthy proofs make the existing evidence easier to inspect. Scientific support is essentially unchanged; removal of the conditional code-release statement and stronger causal wording without new tests limit the gain.
